title: Incremental provenance metrics for output shards and redaction playbook
creator: Ravi Kapoor
description:
Problem: As we scale streamed responses with tool/function calls and structured outputs, engineering and SRE teams need deterministic provenance and privacy-safe telemetry for partial outputs (what we call output shards). Current metrics emit per-request aggregates which obscure tail latency and the source of PII that may appear mid-stream. This ticket designs and implements a lightweight provenance and redaction playbook for incremental output units (shards) so operators can debug latency/cost regressions without exposing sensitive content.

Goals:
- Assign stable provenance IDs to output shards that survive retries and can be linked to tracing spans and tool-call metadata.
- Emit per-shard metrics (latency percentiles, token counts, KV-cache hits, tool-call counts) with backpressure-aware sampling to avoid cardinality explosion.
- Introduce a dual-path redaction system: (1) an inline token-window scrubber for high-throughput low-latency paths, and (2) an async deep-scan redaction step for audit logs and long-term storage.
- Provide an operational playbook (how to interpret shard metrics, when to enable deep-scan, when to raise PII incidents).
acceptance_criteria: Each streamed output shard is assigned a stable provenance_id that appears in traces and emitted metrics for the lifetime of the request.
Per-shard metrics emitted for latency, tokens, kv_cache_hit, and tool_call_count, visible in console dashboards under 'Streaming -> Shards'.
Adaptive sampling reduces metric cardinality for high-volume customers while preserving 99th-percentile accuracy within 3% for sampled telemetry.

Inline scrubber removes high-confidence PII (emails, SSNs, credit-card patterns) from logs before they leave the host; deep-scan redaction runs in background for audit logs with a configurable retention policy.
Playbook document published with runbooks for PII findings and steps to correlate shard provenance IDs to GitHub PR or model rollout metadata.
implementation_notes:
Design choices considered: 1) Attach provenance_id as a short stable hash of (request_id, shard_index, routing_epoch) to minimize storage cost and leak surface. Trade-off: deterministic hash could be linkable; mitigate by mixing a rotation salt per-deployment. 2) Emit per-shard metrics via our existing metric-agent but tag metrics with sampled_provenance=true/false to allow downstream rollups. 3) Inline scrubber implemented as a lightweight DFA-based pattern matcher to preserve latency; deep-scan uses the existing PII classifier service asynchronously. 4) For tool-calls we propagate span baggage with tool_name and call_index so shard -> tool attribution is straightforward.

Implementation plan: prototype in streaming runtime branch, add feature flag 'shard_provenance_v1', add console panel and KQL queries for early users, iterate on sampling thresholds after 2 weeks of canary telemetry.

Open trade-offs: cardinality vs. debuggability, deterministic IDs vs. privacy risk, inline scrubber false negatives vs. async deep-scan cost.
comments: 2025-02-11 - Ravi Kapoor: Initial write-up and design sketch uploaded. Chose short provenance_id format to avoid index bloat. Asked infra to validate storage cost estimate.
2025-02-12 - Maya Chen: Reviewed offline. Asked that provenance salt be rotated weekly and exposed in audit logs only. Raised concern about sampling skew for multi-tenant hosts.

2025-02-14 - Linh Tran (SRE): Ran a cost simulation for per-shard metric cardinality at 1k reqs/s with avg 6 shards/req — estimated metric cardinality growth of ~12x. Proposed adaptive reservoir sampling per customer.

2025-02-16 - Security review (group): Flagged deterministic provenance hash as a privacy surface. Recommended adding per-deployment salt and a reversible mapping stored only in KMS-backed vault for incident lookups.
2025-02-17 - Maya Chen: Implemented feature flag gating and updated acceptance criteria to include console visibility. Assigned PRs for runtime and console after triage.
2025-02-18 - QA (Jamal Ortiz): Smoke tests added for inline scrubber; found a false positive with date patterns — created follow-up ENG-27699 to harden date regexes.
notes_for_release: Feature shipped behind feature flag. Console panel under 'Streaming -> Shards' in runtime-1.22. Customers can opt-in via project-level flag. Default sampling applied to free-tier tenants.
next_steps: Merge PRs and deploy canary to us-west-2 with 10% traffic
Monitor sampled provenance accuracy and adjust adaptive sampling thresholds
Publish playbook and notify CSMs for early adopters
